sources.entry: Polaris - Music browsing and streaming application optimized for large music collections, ease of use and high performance. MIT Rust/Docker

summary.one_liner: Polaris is a free, open-source, self-hosted music streaming server for browsing and listening to a music collection from computers and mobile devices.
summary.what_it_does: Polaris runs as a self-hosted server that streams a music library to any computer or mobile device. It supports flac, mp3, mp4, mpc, ogg, opus, ape, wav and aiff files. Music can be browsed by album, artist or genre, or as a file tree. The README also mentions song waveform visualization, multi-value metadata fields (such as multiple artists per song), and per-field search queries. Multiple users can each have their own playlists. Configuration is a plain-text file that can also be edited through the built-in UI. The server API is documented via OpenAPI and served by each installation.
use_cases: stream a personal music library to phone or laptop
browse a large music collection by album, artist or genre
manage per-user playlists for a household
search music metadata by specific fields
how_to_run: Install from the Installation documentation linked in the README (Windows, Linux, BSD, or Docker)
notable: Designed for large collections, stated goal of 100,000+ songs
Runs on Windows, Linux, BSD, or Docker
Browse by tags or as a file tree
Built-in UI for editing plain-text configuration
Companion Polaris Android app, plus third-party iOS and other clients named in the README
caveats: Installation details are in external documentation, not the README itself
Mobile apps listed are separate projects; the README names Polaris Android and third-party clients only
